messages:
Ana (eng-platform): Quick sync — we need to pick a shape for internal API routing: lightweight bridge (proto->json passthrough) vs a smart gateway that owns routing, quotas, and telemetry. Impacts: latency, rollout UX, observability. cc @Mike P., @Sabrina R., @Jia L. :thinking:

Mike P.: Leaning toward a thin bridge + strong internal gRPC. Gateway should stay thin (auth, ingress validation). Decision logic in platform/sidecars. Smart gateway adds ~2-10ms and becomes a config/code hotspot. Envoy filters + rate-limit service covers quotas fine.

Sabrina R.: I'm worried about rollout UX. A smart gateway centralizes canary/percentage routing and makes rollouts simpler for product teams. Sidecars distribute that complexity back to many teams. Sidecar gives locality but more deployment surface.

Jia L.: Telemetry note: whichever path we pick must preserve consistent attributes for cost attribution/tracing: customer_id, model_variant, route_key, latency_ms. If the gateway terminates proto we need to forward those attributes downstream. Sidecars require uniform sampling/collector config so traces are joinable.

Mike P.: From the POC numbers (very rough): internal gRPC proto path p50 ~0.9ms, JSON edge + bridge p50 ~2.5ms, full smart-gateway routing with policy eval p50 ~6-12ms depending on rules. p95 gaps widen but depend on batch/cache. If latency budget is tight, favor thin gateway.

Sabrina R.: SDK/backwards compatibility is also important — customers expect simple REST at the edge. If we make internals proto-first, the bridge must keep JSON stable or we provide codegen. PLG signups are sensitive to small client breakages.

Ana (eng-platform): Proposal: hybrid approach — thin gateway for ingress (auth, validation, basic rate-limits), sidecar per tenant/node for model-variant decisions + telemetry tagging. Rollout UX: header-based canary + percentage routing controlled by config service and feature flags. Fallback plan: variant A -> variant B -> global fallback.

Mike P.: +1. Implementation idea: gateway does header enrichment and simple routing, sidecar has the policy engine (percent-based routing, latency-based fallback). We'll keep canonical attributes in headers: `x-tenant-id`, `x-model-variant`, `x-route-key`, `x-cost-center`. Envoy ext_auth + rate_limit ext config for quota checks.

Sabrina R.: That keeps rollouts ergonomic while limiting gateway complexity. We should define a telemetry surface contract (required fields, event types, sampling). I'll volunteer to draft the UX for canary controls in Console.

Ana (eng-platform): I'll open an RFC tomorrow. Quick example config for percentage routing I'm thinking of:

```yaml
routing:
  rules:
    - name: canary-header
      match: header('x-canary') == 'true'
      variant: v2
      weight: 100
    - name: tenant-percent
      match: tenant_pct(5) # 5% of tenants
      variant: v2
      weight: 5
    - name: default
      variant: v1
```

Jia L.: Tracing: propagate W3C traceparent/span across gateway->sidecar->model runtime. Make sure we don't drop sampling flags during proto<->json translation. Also add a small event when we switch variants (helps debugging).

Mike P.: I'll add Envoy filters for header passthrough, rate-limit hook, and a bench harness for p50/p95 numbers across the hybrid flow. Will post numbers to the RFC. :+1:

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: routing-prototype -> staging at 2026-03-22T02:00Z

Ana (eng-platform): Great — thanks all. Action items: I'll file RFC + telemetry contract draft; Sabrina owns rollout UX mock; Mike owns envoy filters + bench. Tagging @Sabrina R. to confirm Console controls. :thumbsup:
